investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Agent Provisioning Evals
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-09-05T12:30–12:31Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm provisioning gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2) was unreachable. Because the failure occurs at the very first POST /api/agents call and all sibling checks share the exact same error message, the swarm gateway is the single shared upstream dependency whose unavailability caused every required evidence field (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to go uncollected.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway backing POST /api/agents (routed through an AWS ELB in us-east-2) returned HTTP 502 with error code bad_gateway during agent provisioning. Because agent creation is the prerequisite step for all three remote-agents checks, none of them could advance past the createAgent call, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing every check to fail with the same message. This is an eval-observed infrastructure availability failure localized to the swarm gateway / ELB endpoint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.
